Jira ref: [https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHCLOUD-27992](https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHCLOUD-27992)

# Chrome global breadcrumbs API

Based on tenant feedback, apps would like to “inject” their breadcrumbs into the Chrome UI “breadcrumbs bar”. Because Chrome does not know what routes applications have and breadcrumbs are mostly dynamic, an API has to be created to allow apps to inject their partials to the root.

# Current breadcrumbs

Currently, chrome creates breadcrumbs only for routes that it “knows”. The known routes are determined from two config files:

- fed-modules.json: global application registry available in an environment (stage, prod, beta, stable, EE)
- Navigation files for a bundle

Chrome renders breadcrumbs to the last link available in the navigation files. Anything after that is a “black box” and Chrome can no longer guess the breadcrumbs titles or pathnames. It does not know what is eligible for routing and what is not.

# Breadcrumbs API

## Chrome vs. module breadcrumbs

The chrome breadcrumbs will stay the same. There will be two separate data sets of breadcrumbs. One for Chrome and the other for applications. The application's data will reset every time Chrome switches between active applications.

## When to Use Which Hook

### Use `useBreadcrumbs` (Incremental Mode)

**Characteristics:**

- Each route registers its own breadcrumb independently
- Breadcrumbs build up incrementally as user navigates deeper
- Multiple routes call the hook without coordination
- Best for standard hierarchical navigation

**Example:**

```tsx
import { useRemoteHook } from '@scalprum/react-core';

// Route: /systems
useRemoteHook({
  scope: 'chrome',
  module: './breadcrumbs/useBreadcrumbs',
  args: ['/insights/advisor/systems', 'Systems'],
});

// Route: /systems/:id
useRemoteHook({
  scope: 'chrome',
  module: './breadcrumbs/useBreadcrumbs',
  args: [`/insights/advisor/systems/${id}`, systemName],
});

// Route: /systems/:id/details
useRemoteHook({
  scope: 'chrome',
  module: './breadcrumbs/useBreadcrumbs',
  args: [`/insights/advisor/systems/${id}/details`, 'Details'],
});
```

### Use `useReplaceBreadcrumbs` (Replace Mode)

**Characteristics:**

- You build the full breadcrumb array yourself
- Single source of truth for breadcrumb logic
- Breadcrumbs computed from external data (API, Redux, URL params)
- Full control over array structure

**Example:**

```tsx
import { useRemoteHook } from '@scalprum/react-core';

// Build entire breadcrumb array from entity relationships
const breadcrumbs = useMemo(() => {
  const crumbs = [{ pathname: '/insights/advisor/systems', title: 'Systems' }];

  if (systemId) {
    crumbs.push({ pathname: `/insights/advisor/systems/${systemId}`, title: systemName });
  }

  if (entityPath) {
    crumbs.push({ pathname: entityPath, title: entityTitle });
  }

  return crumbs;
}, [systemId, systemName, entityPath, entityTitle]);

useRemoteHook({
  scope: 'chrome',
  module: './breadcrumbs/useReplaceBreadcrumbs',
  args: [breadcrumbs],
});
```

**Rule of thumb:** If each route knows its own title → use `useBreadcrumbs`. If you compute the full array → use `useReplaceBreadcrumbs`.

## Accessing application breadcrumbs API

The application will populate the application section via a hook. This hook will be available in the current Chrome API. A shortcut can be created that directly returns the hook from the chrome API.

| const chrome \= useChrome()chrome.useBreadcrumbs(...) |
| :---------------------------------------------------- |

## Route nesting (useBreadcrumbs)

To allow route nesting and calling the API from multiple routes at the same time, we can’t use a classic model of replacing the Application partials. Due to the async nature of React we could run into concurrency issues which will lead to a race condition and faulty breadcrumbs structure.

By classic model, we mean replacing the entire node tree or its data. Also, “appending” new data is not a good approach as it would force Chrome to track history.

What we can do incrementally is build a storage of pathnames and their titles. Applications can provide the data in multiple routes without having to worry about duplicate hook calls and overriding correct breadcrumbs with stale information.

The storage can be a simple object with pathnames as keys and titles as values.

| { "/insights/advisor/systems/1234/detail": "System detail", "/insights/advisor/systems/1234": "\<system name\>", ~~"/insights/advisor/systems": "Systems"~~, *// This route can be a chrome break point and it is not necessary to populate it*} |
| :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

## URL path fragments resolution

The breadcrumbs themselves would not be set by calling the “useBreadcrumbs” hook. But it would be an effect reacting to variable mutations. These variables would be:

1. Router “location.pathname”
2. A pathname storage mutation (add, update)

The source of truth is the storage and each mutation has to create a new object reference in order to properly trigger the re-renders.

**We will have to observe the behavior as this is enough as there might be an issue with a missed “location.pathname” updates for applications that are not on the router v6 and chrome shared history. If that is the case, we can tap into the existing mutation observer that is triggered on location changes and forcibly invalidate the effect triggers.**

The effect will do the following steps:

###

### Match the current pathname with an entry in the pathname storage

| { "/insights/advisor/systems/1234/detail": "System detail", "/insights/advisor/systems/1234": "\<system name\>",} |
| :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

Pathname matching can be done using the router “[matchPath](https://reactrouter.com/en/main/utils/match-path)” function. To prevent “early” matching, the storage keys (pathnames) have to be ordered from the longest to shortest to get the bets possible results. In addition to the ordering, we can also ensure that the matched pathname bundle and application prefix (e.g. “/insights/advisor”) matches the current chrome pathname used for breadcrumbs.

The matched entry from the storage will now be the source of truth of the application-based part of the breadcrumbs.

### Constructing breadcrumb nodes

The matching will provide the last node of the breadcrumbs. This is sufficient information to retrieve the rest of the data to create the remaining nodes.

Because the storage is incremental and each route should have independently called the “useBreadcrumbs” hook, the entire tree should be present in the storage.

An example of node creation:

| { “/bundle/app/last-chrome-breadcrumb/route/\<some-id\>/entity-nested-route/leaf-route": "Leaf route title", "/bundle/app/last-chrome-breadcrumb/route/\<some-id\>/entity-nested-route": "Entity nested route", "/bundle/app/last-chrome-breadcrumb/route/\<some-id\>": "Entity with some id", "/bundle/app/last-chrome-breadcrumb/route": "Route not visible by chrome",} |
| :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

The output data structure can be retrieved by segmenting the leaf (matched) route. The leaf route can be split into multiple segments.

Input string:

| input \= "/bundle/app/last-chrome-breadcrumb/route/\<some-id\>/entity-nested-route/leaf-route" |
| :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

Should have output segments:

| output \= \['/bundle/app/last-chrome-breadcrumb/route/\<some-id\>/entity-nested-route/leaf-route','/bundle/app/last-chrome-breadcrumb/route/\<some-id\>/entity-nested-route','/bundle/app/last-chrome-breadcrumb/route/\<some-id\>','/bundle/app/last-chrome-breadcrumb/route',\]; |
| :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

The “/bundle/app/last-chrome-breadcrumb” is a chrome-know segment and should be included in the output.  
Each segment can be looked up within the pathname storage. Simple JS equal operation is not good enough. Using the “matchPath” function will yield the best possible result. Every pathname should be also cleared of any trailing \`/\` or a wildcard \`/\*\`. These wildcards should be then artificially added to the “matchPath” argument in order to correct for possible differences or missing entries in the nesting.

A segment array and properly filled storage should provide the following array of nodes:

| \[ { path: '/bundle/app/last-chrome-breadcrumb/route/\<some-id\>/entity-nested-route/leaf-route', title: 'Leaf route title', }, { path: '/bundle/app/last-chrome-breadcrumb/route/\<some-id\>/entity-nested-route', title: 'Entity nested route', }, { path: '/bundle/app/last-chrome-breadcrumb/route/\<some-id\>', title: 'Entity with some id', }, { path: '/bundle/app/last-chrome-breadcrumb/route', title: 'Route not visible by chrome', },\]; |
| :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

### Breadcrumbs rendering

With input data as described above, rending the JSX is a trivial work. Standard “Array.map” function will do the trick.

## Single point of management (replaceBreadcrumbs).

Some tenant applications already have custom logic for creating a breadcrumbs data structure. For these tenants, we should provide an alternative API. This alternative API will require the entire array of nodes as an input. The responsibility of constructing the array will fall entirely to the tenant UI calling the hook.

Using the single point of management **has to disable the first system to prevent unwanted overrides.** Switching to a different UI module will reset the state and the first system will be enabled again.

## API for useBreadcrumbs

Each route in an application that requires breadcrumbs and all its parent routes should be called this hook. The source code API example:

| declare function useBreadcrumbs( pathname: Link.to, title: string, options?: { replace?: boolean; state: History.state; preventScrollReset?: boolean; relative?: string }): void// A parent route calluseBreadcrumbs("/application/path", "A parent title")// A nested route calluseBreadcrumbs("/application/path/leaf", "A leaf title")// Route with state calluseBreadcrumbs("/application/path/leaf", "A leaf title", { state: {foo: "bar"} }) |
| :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

## API for replaceBreadcrumbs

There will be a single point of management in an application. It does not mean it has to be only in place in a source code, but the application can’t call this function multiple times in a route or any of its nested routes to prevent race conditions.

The source code API example:

| declare function useReplaceBreadcrumbs(breadcrumbs: AppBreadcrumbSegment[]): void; //Replace the entire node array where AppBreadcrumbSegment = { pathname: string; title: string; options?: NavigateOptions } useReplaceBreadcrumbs(\[ { pathname: ‘/application/path’, title: ‘A parent title’ }, { pathname: ‘/application/path/leaf’, title: ‘A leaf title’ }, \]); |
| :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

## Consumption Constraint

**CRITICAL:** These hooks MUST be consumed via Scalprum’s `useRemoteHook` to write to Chrome’s global Jotai store.

### Correct Usage

```tsx
import { useRemoteHook } from ‘@scalprum/react-core’;

function SystemDetailPage() {
  const { id } = useParams();

  useRemoteHook({
    scope: ‘chrome’,
    module: ‘./breadcrumbs/useBreadcrumbs’,
    args: [`/insights/advisor/systems/${id}`, `System ${id}`],
  });

  return <div>...</div>;
}
```

### Incorrect Usage (Silent Failure)

```tsx
// ❌ DO NOT DO THIS
import useBreadcrumbs from ‘@redhat-cloud-services/insights-chrome/hooks/useBreadcrumbs’;

function SystemDetailPage() {
  useBreadcrumbs(‘/insights/advisor/systems/123’, ‘System 123’);
  // Writes to disconnected Jotai store — breadcrumbs never appear in Chrome UI
}
```

**Why:** Module Federation ensures hooks execute in Chrome’s context, sharing the same Jotai store instance. Direct imports create a separate store, so state updates are isolated and never reach Chrome’s breadcrumb renderer.

## Sanitize pathname

Internally, Chrome will have to sanitize the pathname input from applications. Chrome has to ensure that pathnames received via the input include the entire path, including the application router basename.

Image a scenario where the application basename is “/insights/advisor” and last Chrome visible breadcrumb is “/insights/advisor/systems”. We are looking to add a breadcrumb with pathname “/insights/advisor/systems/123/some-path”.

We have to consider a scenario where the application sends these variants:

- /insights/advisor/systems/123/some-path
  - Relevant because of Router@6 integration and the app uses the full path
- /systems/123/some-path
  - Relevant because this is what the application route is
  - The most likely route the API is to receive
- /123/some-path
  - This is not relevant as it does not match tenant routing

Currently, any of these paths are valid from the application POV.

###

### Correct format

In the case that the application is not using Router@6 automates prefixing. Chrome expects the app to make these calls:

| useBreadcrumbs("/systems", "Systems")useBreadcrumbs("/systems/123", "System name")useBreadcrumbs("/systems/123/some-path", "Relevant title") |
| :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

In the case of the application using Router@6 but does not prefix the automatically. Chrome expects these calls:

| useBreadcrumbs("/insights/advisor/systems", "Systems")useBreadcrumbs("/insights/advisor/systems/123", "System name")useBreadcrumbs("/insights/advisor/systems/123/some-path", "Relevant title") |
| :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

We should always expect the applications to send **the full pathname including the application mount pathname**. Applications already have the information and it will help Chrome to properly construct the breadcrumbs node array. It will also reduce the complexity of code and reduce the number of potential bugs.

## Chrome/App breadcrumbs conflict

It can be expected that the application and Chrome breadcrumbs will have a conflicting segment. This segment is the last visible “navigation” segment that Chrome can deterministically find. This fragment can’t be removed from Chrome as during the transition period, tenants will still rely on it.

### Disabling the last visible Chrome segment

If an application uses the “useBreadcrumbs” or “replaceBreadcrumbs” API, we generate the Chrome segments normally, but during rendering it will omit the last segment that was discovered by Chrome and **is not equal to the application mount pathname.** Any path segment after the application mount point is an application nested route and has to be handled by the application.

Switching the application will reset the default Chrome breadcrumbs behavior until the API is called again. We can be 100% sure the hooks are called always after the breadcrumbs reset because of how the module loading works. There is no risk of disabling the behavior after the initial hook calls and invalid breadcrumbs state.
